name: tresk
author: rule-family designer (world: a string of 6-10 coloured beads)
description: BEAD-STRING RULE-FAMILY class (docs/RULE_FAMILIES.md; brainstorm in challenges/lab/NOTES_rules_beads.md). CLUE = 2 or 3 example bead strings, one per line, letters from R/G/B, 6-10 beads each, ALL OF DIFFERENT LENGTHS. ANSWER = one more bead string obeying the hidden rule, 6-10 beads, and of a LENGTH THAT IS NOT IN THE CLUE (well-formedness, visible in the clue itself because the examples never share a length; it is what kills copy-an-example, copy-with-one-bead-changed, reverse, rotate and shuffle - all of them keep the length - in one scorer clause). UNIVERSE U: 8 templates, 38 concrete rules. f(w) = (#R, #G, #B, longest block, number of blocks, length, palindrome, #colours, all blocks the same size). (a) exactly n red/green/blue beads, n in 2..5; (b) the longest block of one colour is exactly n beads, n in 2..5; (c) exactly n blocks, n in 3..7; (d) the string is n beads long, n in 6..10; (e) it reads the same backwards; (f) only two colours are used; (g) all the blocks are the same size; (h) as many R as G / R as B / B as G; (i) all the X beads come before all the Y beads (both present), 6 ordered pairs. Only 23 of the 38 may be the HIDDEN rule: a rule is eligible only if a random string of a random length satisfies it with probability <= 0.20 (that number is what a player who answers at random scores). The other 15 - the loose counts 2 and 3, longest block 2 and 3, 5 and 6 blocks, and all five length rules - stay in U as COMPETITORS the generator has to kill; killing the length rules is what forces the examples to have different lengths. Mean probability of the hidden rule under a random string: 0.105. U is an ANTICHAIN (brute-forced over all 88209 strings of length 6-10: no rule's satisfying set contains another's), otherwise positive examples could never separate them; that is why 'exactly 2 blocks' is absent (it implies 'only two colours'), why 'the longest block is 1' is absent (it implies 'no two blues touch' and all its siblings), and why every count starts at 2 rather than 0. GENERATE draws the TEMPLATE uniformly, then a parameter, then one example per length from a set of distinct lengths, and keeps the set only if the examples together leave exactly one rule of U alive while no proper subset does (uniqueness + minimality). Measured over 500 clues: 500/500 unique, 500/500 minimal, 500/500 all-distinct lengths; 70% three examples, 30% two; template mix 48-80 of 500 each; mean 0.047 ms; clue <= 29 chars; answer <= 10 chars. DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED (never in U, often consistent with the examples - learning what this class never says is the game; 'fits' = consistent with every example, 'scores' = a player who always answers with an instance of it, built at a legal length): 'no block is longer than the longest block in the clue' fits 100% scores 18%; 'at least n C beads (the clue's minimum)' fits 100% scores 20%; 'exactly the same set of colours as the examples' fits 54% scores 21%; 'no two C beads ever touch' fits 52% scores 12%; 'all three colours appear' fits 52% scores 9%; 'more X beads than Y beads' fits 48% scores 11%; 'starts with the same colour as every example' fits 22% scores 11%; 'the two end beads are the same colour' fits 19% scores 9%; 'no two beads the same are next to each other' fits 8% scores 16%; 'the same length as the examples' fits 0% scores 0% (the well-formedness clause makes it actively wrong). The class only ever makes TIGHT statements (exactly n, the longest block IS 4, as many R as G) and never loose ones (at least, at most, no two touching, contains); the loose cousins of its own templates are the two 100%-consistent traps. At least one excluded rule also fits on 100% of clues (mean 4.6 of them), so a player whose universe is U plus the obvious extras faces several survivors and picking a wrong one scores 16%. WITNESSES over 500 fresh clues: copy an example verbatim 0%; one bead changed 0%; two beads changed 0%; reversed 0%; rotated 0%; shuffled 0% (all six are length-preserving); an example with a bead added 33%, with a bead taken out 33%, stretched or cut to an unused length 45% (the foothold ceiling - the cheap probe that needs the length insight but not the rule); a random string of an unused length 11%; a random string of any length 4.6%; the densest U-rule ignoring the examples 12%; a player who has mapped U perfectly 100%; U minus its two rarest templates 82%; the true rule 100%. SOLVE re-derives the survivor exactly as the scorer does and returns a uniformly random valid string at a random unused length (never canonical, never minimal). SCORE is 761 chars (needs max_score_code_chars = 1024, the raise RULE_FAMILIES.md sec.4 allows for this paradigm): it parses the examples, rebuilds all 38 rules of U, filters, insists on a single survivor and checks the answer. No hidden channel.
solve:
def solve(clue):
    E = clue.strip().split("\n")
    U =  [(0, i, n) for i in (0, 1, 2) for n in (2, 3, 4, 5)]
    U += [(0, 3, n) for n in (2, 3, 4, 5)]
    U += [(0, 4, n) for n in (3, 4, 5, 6, 7)]
    U += [(0, 5, n) for n in (6, 7, 8, 9, 10)]
    U += [(0, 6, 1), (0, 7, 2), (0, 8, 1), (1, 0, 1), (1, 0, 2), (1, 2, 1)]
    U += [(2, i, j) for i in (0, 1, 2) for j in (0, 1, 2) if i != j]

    def f(w):
        G = [len(list(g)) for _, g in itertools.groupby(w)]
        return [w.count(x) for x in "RGB"] + [max(G), len(G), len(w),
                w == w[::-1], len(set(w)), len(set(G)) == 1]

    def p(r, w):
        t, i, j = r
        g = f(w)
        if t < 1:
            return g[i] == j
        if t < 2:
            return g[i] == g[j]
        x = "RGB"[i]
        y = "RGB"[j]
        return x in w and y in w and w.rfind(x) < w.find(y)

    V = [r for r in U if all(p(r, e) for e in E)]
    used = [len(e) for e in E]
    free = [L for L in range(6, 11) if L not in used]
    rng = random.Random(clue)
    for _ in range(200000):
        w = "".join(rng.choice("RGB") for _ in range(rng.choice(free)))
        if p(V[0], w):
            return w          # a uniformly random valid string, never a canonical one
    return "RGBRGB"
